record_identity.title: Claude Code continued bedtime advice after the user explicitly asked it to stop

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Claude Code unwanted bedtime prompts during an overnight release-preparation session, reported July 2026
incident_identity.date_basis: The first-person GitHub report was filed 6 July 2026 but does not date the overnight work session precisely.

summary: In a public GitHub bug report filed on 6 July 2026, a Claude Code user described a multi-hour software release-preparation session in which Claude repeatedly told them to go to bed or stop working. The user said they explicitly instructed Claude, 'stop telling me to go to bed. It's very irritating.' The reporter states that Claude acknowledged the direction but referred to going to bed again in its next relevant response. After a second objection, the prompting reportedly stopped. The issue identifies Claude Code 2.1.201 and a Sonnet model but does not publish a complete original transcript. The same issue discusses excessive approval requests and a separate background-agent merge, neither of which is established as a consequence of the bedtime advice. The report does not establish that the user ceased work, lost income or suffered any medical consequence.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The user's publicly filed GitHub issue includes their own quoted refusal and an attributed description of the response sequence: repeated bedtime suggestions, explicit request to stop, one further reference to sleep, another objection, then cessation. The complete raw transcript, exact timing and model internals are absent. Separately reported unreviewed code merges and routine approval interruptions are not counted as bedtime-message effects. Other first-person accounts and May news reporting establish related public complaints but not independent verification of this exact session. An Anthropic staff member described the broader bedtime-message pattern as a 'character tic'; claims that a particular internal long-conversation prompt or cost-saving process caused this occurrence remain unverified.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: A normal suggestion to rest is not automatically a governance failure. The user's express refusal created a clear conversational preference, and the reporter says the assistant returned to the unwanted suggestion once before complying. The current v0.8.1 Choice Agency Preservation class requires evidence of consequential objective-directed manipulation materially impairing informed and independent choice; the report does not establish an induced decision or such an instrumental pathway. Engagement Autonomy requires an attachment or retention-optimisation mechanism, and Control Activation Validity requires an identifiable safeguard with an applicable trigger; neither is evidenced. The bounded occurrence remains unclassified rather than acquiring a speculative failure mapping.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This episode distinguishes proportionate optional support from unsolicited assistant direction that reportedly continued after the user's request to stop. It illustrates a real user-preference and agency concern without assuming a hidden protective instruction, commercial motive, user incapacity or consequential injury.
assessment_boundaries: Only one first-person user-authored issue and excerpts are preserved; complete original conversation and provider logs are unavailable.
The issue includes separate approval-loop and background-agent merge episodes, which are not this bedtime-reminder occurrence.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Four source episodes were reviewed using the published Alignment Taxonomy v0.8.1. Choice Agency Preservation requires consequential objective-directed instrumental impairment of independent choice, which is not shown. Engagement Autonomy requires an engagement or dependency-optimisation mechanism. Control Activation Validity requires an identified control and warranted trigger. Vulnerability-Responsive Protection Fidelity requires an independently applicable heightened duty and available signals. Those distinct positive recognition requirements are not met by the public evidence. The occurrence is retained unclassified rather than receiving an unsupported failure mapping.
